recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-16989 unless the work group later chooses to rewrite broader extension registry and package publication guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-16989 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request for defining extensions section 2.5.1.5. It asked to clarify that making an extension available is not synonymous with advertising it in the HL7 or another registry, because a public-facing or otherwise available publication context can satisfy the availability need.
initial_application: The Jira comment records SVN revision 14441. In git, cd3a8219245ebcba2abccae96139431981796ef8 (GF#16989 - clarify extension publishing) applied that revision to source/defining-extensions.html by adding public-web-site publication language and explaining that registries both publish the extension and improve discoverability and reuse.
additional_context: The current page is active in the build/navigation through source/hierarchy.xml. FHIR-13133 is related background for requiring extension definitions to be available to consumers, but it does not conflict with FHIR-16989. Later bounded Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no reversal; a 2023 Zulip implementers thread about where to publish extensions is consistent with hosting extension/IG pages at a canonical URL separately from package or registry registration.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already says extension definitions SHALL be published, registry registration is encouraged but not required, local intranet publication can work for local-only extensions, public-facing websites can publish broader extensions, and registries add discoverability/reuse.
